tagline: South Korea's second city curves around sandy beaches, seafood markets and hillside villages, with a temple on the sea cliffs and Asia's biggest film festival every autumn.
overview: Busan is Korea's largest port and second-largest city, spread between mountains and the sea on the peninsula's southeastern tip. Its neighbourhoods climb steep hillsides above the harbour, linked by tunnels, bridges and the Gwangan Bridge that lights up over the bay at night.

The city is best known for its beaches. Haeundae is the busiest, lined with hotels and towers, while Gwangalli has bridge views and a lively café strip. Jagalchi Market, on the waterfront, is the country's largest seafood market, where you can pick fish downstairs and have it cooked upstairs.

Away from the sea, the pastel houses of Gamcheon Culture Village stack up a hillside once settled by refugees during the Korean War, and Haedong Yonggungsa Temple sits right on the coastal rocks. Every October the Busan International Film Festival fills the Centum City district.

funFacts.title: KOREA'S BIGGEST PORT
funFacts.text: Busan handles most of South Korea's container shipping and is one of the busiest ports in the world.

funFacts.title: A WARTIME CAPITAL
funFacts.text: During the Korean War, Busan served as the temporary capital of South Korea.

funFacts.title: SIX BEACHES IN ONE CITY
funFacts.text: Haeundae, Gwangalli, Songjeong, Songdo, Dadaepo and Ilgwang beaches are all within the city.

funFacts.title: A REFUGEE VILLAGE TURNED ART
funFacts.text: Gamcheon Culture Village was built by war refugees and later repainted by local artists.

funFacts.title: A TEMPLE BY THE SEA
funFacts.text: Haedong Yonggungsa is one of the few Korean temples built right on the seashore.

funFacts.title: ASIA'S BIG FILM FESTIVAL
funFacts.text: The Busan International Film Festival, held each October since 1996, is one of Asia's most important.

funFacts.title: PICK IT, THEN EAT IT
funFacts.text: At Jagalchi Market you choose seafood on the ground floor and restaurants upstairs cook it for you.

funFacts.title: A BRIDGE THAT GLOWS
funFacts.text: The 7.4-km Gwangan Bridge is lit with changing LED light shows after dark.

funFacts.title: HOT SPRINGS IN TOWN
funFacts.text: The Haeundae and Dongnae areas have natural hot springs that have been used for centuries.

funFacts.title: THE CITY'S OWN SOUP
funFacts.text: Dwaeji gukbap, a pork and rice soup, is Busan's signature comfort food.
